Function map

Source: vignettes/articles/function-map.Rmd
function-map.Rmd

This page maps the functions of mortensor onto the steps of an analysis and shows how their results feed into each other. Each box names a function and its main purpose. Paths through the maps are workflows; the section “What is not covered” lists steps that need other tools.

The main path

Every analysis passes the same objects from left to right. Functions in the boxes create the objects; the labels on the arrows are the functions that connect them.

flowchart TD
  T["`**your tables**
  deaths, populations or exposures (CSV, Excel, official exports)`"]
  D["`**mt_data object**
  observations at any age and period resolution, strata`"]
  S["`**model specification**
  lee_carter(), li_lee(), rwd(), ... and wrappers ensemble(), reconciled()`"]
  F["`**mt_fit**
  estimates per stratum or joint`"]
  P["`**mt_draws**
  simulated paths of future rates`"]
  B["`**mt_backtest**
  scores of past forecasts`"]
  R["`**tables and plots**
  life expectancy, rates, deaths, gaps, inequality indices`"]
  T -- "mt_data()" --> D
  D -- "prepare and check (map 1)" --> D
  D -- "mt_fit(spec, data, prep)" --> F
  S --> F
  F -- "mt_forecast()" --> P
  P -- "map 3" --> R
  D -- "mt_backtest(spec, data, prep)" --> B
  B -- "mt_score()" --> R
  D -- "mt_observed(): the past" --> R

Map 1: from tables to analysis-ready data

Each step is an analysis decision. Most data sets need only some of them.

flowchart TD
  subgraph READ["Read"]
    A1["`**mt_data()**
    deaths, exposures, populations in long
    or wide tables; age labels such as 85+,
    '85 years and over', '85 Jahre und mehr';
    suppression symbols; totals and unknown
    ages handled with warnings`"]
    A2["`**mt_read_genesis(), mt_read_gbe()**
    German official exports`"]
    A3["`**mt_from_hmd(), as_mt_data()**
    Human Mortality Database, StMoMo,
    demography objects`"]
  end
  subgraph PREP["Prepare (decisions)"]
    B1["`**mt_as_exposure(type)**
    person-years from mid-year,
    1 January or 31 December populations`"]
    B2["`**mt_subset()**
    ages, years, strata to analyse`"]
    B3["`**mt_group_levels(), mt_relabel()**
    aggregation layers: cause groups,
    quintiles, regions; recode labels`"]
    B4["`**mt_fill_suppressed()**
    estimate suppressed counts from
    published totals or known bounds`"]
  end
  subgraph CHECK["Check"]
    C1["`**mt_validate()**
    impossible values, missing cells,
    totals among levels, sums of a hierarchy`"]
  end
  subgraph HARM["Harmonise resolution"]
    H1["`**mt_regroup()**
    common age groups or years
    ('deaths', 'common')`"]
    H2["`**mt_ungroup()**
    single years from age groups
    (penalised composite link)`"]
    H3["`**mt_smooth()**
    smooth rates over age, time or both
    (P-splines, Whittaker, GAM);
    mt_smooth_check(), mt_plot_smooth()`"]
    H4["`**mt_prep() with step_*()**
    the same steps inside fits
    and backtests, without leakage`"]
  end
  A1 --> B1
  A2 --> B1
  A3 --> B2
  B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> C1
  C1 --> H1
  C1 --> H2
  H2 --> H3
  H1 --> M["model-ready mt_data"]
  H3 --> M
  H4 -.-> M

Map 2: models, coherence and evaluation 

flowchart TD
  M["model-ready mt_data"]
  subgraph ONE["Models for one population per stratum"]
    direction LR
    S1["`**lee_carter()**

    S3["`**hyndman_ullah(), stmomo(),

  end

    direction LR

    common trend, bounded deviations`"]
    J2["`**product_ratio(), tucker3(),
    cause_shares()**
    other joint and cause models`"]
  end
  subgraph WRAP["Wrappers around any model"]
    direction LR
    W1["`**ensemble()**
    mixture of models,
    better calibrated`"]
    W2["`**reconciled(model, hierarchy)**
    totals and parts add up
    draw by draw`"]
    W3["`**bootstrapped(), tuned()**
    parameter uncertainty,
    inner tuning`"]
    W4["`**calibrated(model, years = 10)**

  H["`**mt_hierarchy(), mt_aggregate_strata()**

  mt_jump_off() reports the first-year step`"]
  M --> FIT
  H --> W2
  ONE --> WRAP
  MANY --> WRAP
  ONE --> FIT
  MANY --> FIT
  WRAP --> FIT
  FIT --> INS
  FIT --> FC

What is not covered

These steps of a mortality analysis need other tools or are open development points:

  • Population projections. mortensor forecasts death rates; future exposures (for expected deaths) come from a population projection, for example of the statistical office, passed as exposure.
  • Spatial models for small areas. There is no model with spatial smoothing between neighbouring regions (such as BYM models); pooling works through common trends (li_lee()); Bayesian APC models smooth over age, period and cohort within each stratum.
  • Uncertainty of score differences. mt_score() reports mean scores; standard errors over origins and strata or paired tests of two models are not computed.
  • Lifespan variation. Lifespan variation (e-dagger, Gini) is not a built-in quantity; mt_decompose() accepts it as a function of the rates.
  • Multiple imputation of suppressed cells. mt_fill_suppressed() returns one estimate; the uncertainty of suppressed counts is not carried into forecasts.
  • Causes of death with changing coding. ICD revisions and coding changes (for example of dementia) are not bridged; cause groups that span the affected codes reduce the problem.
